item.title: Paraguay's former president faces prosecutors after his removal over bank collapse
item.description:
Paraguay's former president faces prosecutors after his removal over bank collapse
Paraguay's former President Santiago Peña has been taken to the attorney general’s office for questioningByThe Associated PressNovember 7, 2026, 10:45 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
Paraguay’s former president was taken to the attorney general’s office for questioning Saturday, just hours after being ousted by Congress over the collapse of a major bank. The Central Bank said it was working to compensate hundreds of thousands of people who were locked out of their accounts this week.
Drone footage taken by Paraguay’s Telefuturo showed ousted President Santiago Peña arriving at the attorney general’s compound in a black SUV, escorted by police officers. He wore navy blue pants and a white shirt and was not handcuffed.
Paraguayan prosecutors on Friday ordered the arrest of Peña and former Central Bank chief Carlos Carvallo as part of a criminal investigation into alleged breach of trust and other offenses tied to the collapse of Ueno Bank. Peña was transferred to a military base late Friday as hundreds of protesters gathered outside his home.
The arrest order was issued soon after the Senate removed Peña from office in a unanimous vote. The verdict came just three days after regulators seized Ueno Bank, freezing nearly 3 million customers’ access to their savings and triggering a political crisis.
Peña was replaced by Vice President Pedro Alliana, who began naming a new Cabinet Saturday. The Central Bank said Saturday that 1.2 million Ueno customers had received partial or full reimbursement of their insured deposits under Paraguayan law.
Lawmakers accused Peña of using his political influence to steer hundreds of millions of dollars in public funds into Ueno while regulators overlooked risky insider lending. Peña has denied wrongdoing.

item.title: Pakistani astronaut to board Shenzhou 24 and become the first foreigner on China's space station
item.description:
Pakistani astronaut to board Shenzhou 24 and become the first foreigner on China's space station
A Pakistani astronaut will board China’s Shenzhou 24 spacecraft as the first foreign national on Beijing’s space stationByThe Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 11:34 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BEIJING -- A Pakistani astronaut will join the crew of China's Shenzhou 24 spacecraft on a mission that would make him the first foreign national to board Beijing's space station, state media reported Saturday.
According to the China Manned Space Agency, the Pakistani astronaut would complete a short on-orbit flight and then return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou 23 spacecraft, China's official news agency Xinhua reported, without specifying the launch date.
The mission would mark the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program, it said.
Earlier this year, Xinhua reported that two Pakistani candidates, Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, started their training alongside their Chinese counterparts, and the plan was that one of them would be selected as a payload specialist for a short-term spaceflight mission.

The upcoming flight is part of an agreement signed by China and Pakistan in February 2025.
China is preparing for its first crewed lunar landing by 2030. The U.S. is seen as China’s top space rival, with NASA aiming to land astronauts on the lunar surface in 2028.

item.title: Diwali celebrations coincide with worsening air. Here’s how to stay safer
item.description:
Diwali celebrations coincide with worsening air. Here’s how to stay safer
For people across South Asia, especially in northern India, Diwali celebrations coincide with the return of hazardous winter air, raising concerns about how to celebrate safelyBySIBI ARASU Associated PressNovember 6, 2026, 9:27 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
BENGALURU, India -- For people across South Asia, especially in northern India, Diwali celebrations coincide with the return of hazardous winter air, raising concerns about how to celebrate safely.
Winter also brings severe smog to parts of Pakistan and China, where warmer air can act as a lid, trapping colder air and pollution near the ground. In eastern Europe, burning coal and wood to heat homes also adds to winter pollution. Western Hemisphere countries, meanwhile, face their own seasonal air-quality problems, as summer wildfires send smoke across vast areas of the United States and Canada.
Experts say no matter where you live or when you face pollution, simple steps such as checking the air quality index, wearing a well-fitting mask and using air purifiers can reduce exposure to harmful pollutants.
An estimated 1 billion people worldwide celebrate Diwali, a holiday of Hindus and Jains with ties to ancient epics such as the Ramayana. Fireworks traditionally set off during the holiday, which starts Sunday, can make polluted air more dangerous.
As Diwali approaches, here are ways to reduce exposure to polluted air.
Fireworks add a sharp burst of pollution to a much bigger problem. Across India, Pakistan and other parts of South Asia, traffic, factories, dust from construction and burning of crop residues and waste foul the air. Weak winds and stagnant winter air allow that pollution to build up.
“Poor air quality is our all-year-round problem in our country,” said Shweta Narayan, a public health expert at the Global Climate and Health Alliance. Narayan said firecrackers add to the problem.

item.title: 2 trains crash in Egypt; 2 dead, more than 100 injured
item.description:
2 trains crash in Egypt; 2 dead, more than 100 injured
Egypt's railway system has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance.ByThe Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 9:04 AM
CAIRO -- Seven people were killed and over 100 others injured when two trains collided Sunday south of the Egyptian capital, Cairo, the Chief Prosecutor’s office said in a statement. It also said the train’s conductor was among those killed.
The crash occurred in al-Ayyat district in Giza province, about 52 kilometers (32 miles) south of Cairo, when a train traveling to the southwestern Fayoum province crashed into the rear of a train heading to the southern province of Aswan, according to the Transportation Ministry.
The Chief Prosecutor's office said late Sunday its investigators had arrived at the site. An inspection indicated that the crash took place when the Giza-Fayyoum train collided with the last carriage of the Cairo-Aswan train, that was stationary on the same track and traveling in the same direction, officials said.
Train derailments and crashes are common in Egypt, where the railway system which has a history of mismanagement and poor maintenance of equipment. In recent years, the government announced modernization initiatives to improve its railways.
Ayman Gamal, a resident of Kafr Girza in al-Ayyat where the crash occurred, said people living nearby rushed to the scene, pulled out survivors and called ambulances,
Gamal said that he saw around 80 of the injured were taken by ambulances to nearby hospitals. Some passengers were trapped inside one of the carriages of the stationary train and were dead when they were pulled out, he said.

item.title: Russia targets emergency crews at the site of a deadly strike in southern Ukraine
item.description:
Russia targets emergency crews at the site of a deadly strike in southern Ukraine
A Russian drone has struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern UkraineByVASILISA STEPANENKO Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 5:20 AM
ZAPORIZHZHIA, Ukraine -- A Russian drone struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern Ukraine on Sunday, hitting a former school and nearby shelter that had been earlier blasted by multiple Russian guided bombs as residents waited for humanitarian aid, authorities said.
No one was injured in Sunday’s strike on the village of Komyshuvakha, but specialized rescue equipment was damaged, according to Ukraine’s State Emergency Service.
Ukraine said Monday's attack on the same location killed at least 55 people, near the front line in the Zaporizhzhia region.
As of Sunday afternoon, 45 people were listed as missing, according to the acting head of the regional military administration, Mykhailo Semikin. Many of the bodies recovered have not been identified and DNA analysis is ongoing.
Village resident Mykola Krasnov, 72, told The Associated Press on Saturday that he was still looking for his wife, but had heard no word from rescuers.
“She went to get humanitarian aid, and a 3-ton bomb was dropped there. Where is she?” he said. “She didn’t come home, and they didn’t find her body there. She isn’t in the morgue, and she isn’t here alive.”
Ukraine has routinely accused Russia of conducting multiple strikes at the same site in quick succession to target emergency crews responding to the initial attack.
On Saturday, police officers and relatives gathered in Zaporizhzhia for a farewell ceremony for six officers killed in Russian strikes on Komyshuvakha, including four who died near the former school.
Rain fell as families wept beside the coffins, and officers held portraits of their fallen colleagues.

item.title: Tourists and locals recount fatal Krakow mass shooting that left Poland reeling
item.description:
Tourists and locals recount fatal Krakow mass shooting that left Poland reeling
Tourists and locals alike witnessed a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, that left six people dead and 15 woundedByRAFAL NIEDZIELSKI Associated Press and CLAUDIA CIOBANU Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 8:21 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
KRAKOW, Poland -- Tourists and locals alike this weekend witnessed a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, that left six people dead and 15 wounded.
The country’s second-largest city is in mourning after a 24-year-old man with far-right views opened fire in Main Square, a major tourist hub, Saturday afternoon. The gunman is in serious condition and also linked to the deaths of his sister and parents at his family home.
Witnesses in Krakow said the violent attack was so surreal, it felt like they were in a film. Polish leaders, visitors and locals praised police officers who shot and wounded the attacker.
Here’s a look at what the witnesses and others said:
— “We literally ran for our lives and managed to hide from the bullets flying around,” Marie-Ange Collaer, a visitor from Brussels, wrote on Facebook. “Lying on the floor in a shop like in a bad police movie whilst you hear bullets everywhere.”
— “We had just walked through the main square and heard the gunshots,” U.K. resident Neil Thaxton wrote on Facebook. “We thought it was fireworks then people started running, we went into a gift shop and the staff took us in the back of the shop and locked the doors and turned the lights off.”
— “In the face of the tragedy in Krakow, we saw the best in people: the courage of police officers, the dedication of paramedics, and the selfless help of ordinary people who rushed to save others," Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote on X. "We are all deeply grateful to them.”

item.title: Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing the Dutch government on Gaza and Israel
item.description:
Tens of thousands march in Amsterdam, pressing the Dutch government on Gaza and Israel
Tens of thousands of people, many dressed in red, have marched through Amsterdam, demanding the Dutch government take stronger action against Israel over GazaByMIKE CORDER Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 10:04 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
AMSTERDAM -- Tens of thousands of people, many of them dressed in red, marched through Amsterdam on Sunday in a mass demonstration aimed at pressing the Dutch government to take more decisive action against Israel over Gaza.
The organizers of “Red Line” demonstrations in the Netherlands called for measures including stricter trade sanctions on Israel, officially declaring that Israel’s actions in Gaza amount to genocide and halting all arms sales to Israel.
The Dutch branch of Amnesty International, one of the organizers, said in an online post that more than 200,000 people joined the march.
“What is happening there is inhumane,” Mike van Dongen said as he walked in the huge throng of people. He was critical of the Dutch government’s actions. “As far as I’m concerned, they are doing nothing,” he said. “They don’t dare take any serious steps.”
As the protesters marched along a normally busy Amsterdam street that was closed to traffic on Sunday, a man stood on a bus stop with a loudspeaker shouting, “Free, free Palestine!” Many of the marchers echoes his cry as they passed.
Israel strongly rejects suggestions it is committing genocide in Gaza in its military campaign that followed the attacks by Hamas-led militants in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023. Militants killed around 1,200 people and took 251 hostages. Israel’s retaliatory offensive has killed tens of thousands of Palestinians and destroyed much of Gaza.

item.title: South Africa's ANC is humbled by its worst election results as it continues its decline
item.description:
South Africa's ANC is humbled by its worst election results as it continues its decline
South Africa’s African National Congress is party facing its worst election results everByGERALD IMRAY Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 10:34 AM
CAPE TOWN, South Africa -- South Africa's African National Congress party faced its worst election results ever Sunday and a new low point on its gradual decline in popularity as voters rebuked it for a failure to deliver basic services like water and electricity in towns and cities.
The once-dominant ANC — the party of Nelson Mandela — had received around 30% of the vote in Wednesday's local government elections with 99% of ballots counted. The final results were expected late on Sunday, according to the Independent Electoral Commission.
The ANC remained the largest party by total share in an election involving hundreds of parties, but the Democratic Alliance that is its main opposition had received around 25% of votes in the near-complete count.
That brought closer to reality the once-unthinkable notion that the ANC that led South Africa out of the white minority rule of apartheid and delivered freedom in 1994 under Mandela might one day not be its biggest party. It used to command 70% of the vote.
The ANC's popularity has declined for more than a decade. It won 45% support in the last local elections in 2021, the first time it had dropped below 50% in any election. In 2024 it then lost its Parliamentary majority for the first time in a national election, which brought about a coalition national government and a seismic shift in South African politics.
The ANC was on course Sunday for a steep drop of about 15 percentage points from the last local elections and the loss of approximately one-third of its support from five years ago.

item.title: Bus overturns on a highway in Croatia, killing at least 2 people and injuring scores
item.description:
Bus overturns on a highway in Croatia, killing at least 2 people and injuring scores
Croatian police say that at least two people were killed and several were injured when a bus overturned on a highwayByThe Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 3:39 AM
Share
ZAGREB, Croatia -- At least two people were killed and several were injured when a bus overturned on a highway in Croatia on Sunday, police said.
The bus with Serbian license plates skidded off the road and overturned at 7:25 a.m. while traveling in the direction of the Croatian capital, Zagreb, police said. The reason for the accident was not immediately clear.
The A3 highway in Croatia leads from the Serbian border, by Zagreb and toward Slovenia.

item.title: Turkey and Azerbaijan deny speculation of fraying relationship
item.description:
Turkey and Azerbaijan deny speculation of fraying relationship
The Turkish and Azerbaijani presidents have reaffirmed the countries’ close ties following speculation of souring relationsByThe Associated PressNovember 8, 2026, 11:40 AM
ISTANBUL -- The Turkish and Azerbaijani presidents reaffirmed their countries’ close ties Sunday in response to growing speculation of souring relations.
Turkey and Azerbaijan are traditional allies with deep cultural and ethnic ties and often describe themselves as being “one nation, two states.” But tensions have emerged recently following criticism in Turkey of Azerbaijan’s decision to ban hijabs in schools and over Baku’s growing ties with Israel.
“Our brotherhood transcends our shared language, history and culture," Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said, speaking at a joint news conference with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in the city of Shusha.
"That is why we see Baku’s joy as Ankara’s joy and Shusha’s pride as the pride of our entire nation,” Erdogan added.
The rift became apparent after social media users in Turkey and some members of Erdogan’s Islamic-oriented ruling party criticized Baku’s decision in September to ban girls and teachers from wearing Islamic covering in schools. Erdogan’s government overturned a similar ban in Turkey after coming to power in 2003. The criticism drew anger in energy-rich Azerbaijan, which complained of interference even though Turkey’s government had made no official statement about the hijab ban.
